artists.biography:
M83 is a French electronic/shoegaze band from Antibes, formed in 2001 by Anthony Gonzalez and Nicolas Fromageau. The band is named after the spiral galaxy Messier 83, and its musical aesthetic is influenced by shoegaze in its extensive use of reverb effects and lyrics spoken softly over loud instrumentals, although M83's songs employ considerably less guitar than most shoegaze bands.
Gonzalez and Fromageau parted ways shortly after touring for their second album Dead Cities, Red Seas & Lost Ghosts, with Gonzalez now recording primarily on his own, often with the help of his brother Yann Gonzalez, vocalist/keyboardist Morgan Kibby, and drummer Loïc Maurin. In 2011, Gonzalez posted an open audition on the M83 website for a multi-instrumentalist who could join the band. 19 year-old Jordan Lawlor won the audition.

apple_music.editorial_notes: M83‘s 10th album wastes no time reorienting you to Anthony Gonzalez’s neon-glow dreamworld, as the opening “Blister Sunrise” instantly plunges you into a synthgaze sound bath as swiftly as “Only Shallow” tosses you straight into the deep end on my bloody valentine’s Loveless. While Gonzalez has long excelled at translating his hallucinatory visions into heart-racing indie-pop anthems, the largely instrumental I Wrote You a Letter feels closer in spirit to his embryonic early-2000s work, where he wasn’t so much singing his heart out as letting his emotions well up into dam-bursting waves of electronic psychedelia. Here, Gonzalez lets the digi-drone drama build to operatic levels (and not just on the track that’s actually called “Opera”). Where “Losing Ground” begins as a serene soundtrack to a new day rising, by the end, its intensifying oscillations feel better suited to accompany a rocket launch. But there are also echoes of Gonzalez’s more esoteric film-score compositions, where his neoclassical and improv affinities come to the fore: If you’re the sort of M83 fan who can’t resist playing air-sax to his signature 2011 synth-pop bop “Midnight City”, you’ll have your work cut out for you when trying to keep up with the mercurial free-jazz meditation “Siren / Behold…Beasts”. Our Favourite Moment: When the gentle psych-folk finger-plucking of “Feeding Time” suddenly explodes into a synth-shocked, speed-prog stomper that sounds like Gonzalez’s tech-topian version of hardcore.

lastfm.wiki_content: “I Wrote You A Letter” is the tenth studio album by French electronic band M83. It was released on September 25, 2026, through lead performer Anthony Gonzalez's own label, Other Suns. It was initially announced, with cover art and tracklist, on 22 July 2026 via the group's official website and their Instagram page. The opening track, "Blister Sunrise", was released as the lead single on September 4. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
“I Wrote You A Letter” is M83’s tenth studio album, a 2026 release that leans into the project’s electronic foundations while also drawing on dream pop, shoegaze, and synth-pop textures. Presented as a more intimate, self-contained work, it was described as a return to the instinctive, bedroom-recording spirit of M83’s early years, with shadowy electronics, ambient passages, and fractured pop forms shaping its sound.

The album’s reception emphasized its small-scale emotional focus and its balance of melody with dense atmospherics. Rather than chasing the widescreen anthemic feel that made M83 a mainstream force, it explores a more personal and reflective mode, while still delivering the layered production and cinematic atmosphere associated with Anthony Gonzalez’s work.
